title: Children and older people as a share of the population
subtitle: Percentage of the population aged under 15 and aged 65 and over, 1950 to 2026.
key_fact: People aged 65 and over made up 16.1% of the population in 2026, compared with 10.7% in 1950.

title: Births and deaths
subtitle: Number of births and deaths registered in Ireland each year, 1989 to 2025.

sources.title: Total Births and Deaths Registered Numbers and Rates (VSA03)

key_fact: 54,125 births and 35,587 deaths were registered in 2025. Births peaked at 75,554 in 2009.

title: Births, deaths and migration
subtitle: People born, people who died, and net migration (people arriving minus people leaving) in the twelve months to April, 1987 to 2026.
key_fact: In the twelve months to April 2026 there were 54,300 births and 35,400 deaths, and net migration added 48,100 people.

title: County populations since 1841
subtitle: Population of each county at each census from 1841 to 2022, as a percentage of its 1841 population. Use the slider to move through the census years.
key_fact: At the 2022 census, 21 of the 26 counties had fewer people than in 1841.

title: Fertility rate
subtitle: Average number of children a woman would have over her lifetime at each year's birth rates, 1969 to 2024.
key_fact: Ireland's fertility rate was 1.47 in 2024, down from 3.85 in 1969. It was last at or above replacement level, 2.1, in 1990.

title: How couples marry
subtitle: Percentage of opposite-sex marriages by type of ceremony, 2000 to 2025.
key_fact: In 2025, 31% of opposite-sex marriages were Catholic ceremonies, down from 80% in 2000. 33% were civil ceremonies.

title: Marriages
subtitle: Number of marriages registered in Ireland each year, 2000 to 2025.
key_fact: 19,898 marriages were registered in 2025, including 624 same-sex marriages. The lowest number was 9,523, in 2020.

title: Population of Ireland
subtitle: Estimated number of people living in the State each April, 1950 to 2026.
key_fact: An estimated 5.53 million people lived in the State in April 2026, up 17% on 2016.

title: New homes completed each year
subtitle: Number of new dwellings completed in Ireland, 2012 to 2025.
key_fact: 36,215 new homes were completed in 2025, compared with 30,124 in 2024.

title: New homes by county
subtitle: New homes completed each year for every 1,000 people living in the county, 2011 to 2025. Use the slider to move through the years.
key_fact: In 2025, Louth had the most new homes for its population, 11.0 for every 1,000 people, and Longford the fewest, at 2.1.

title: People in emergency accommodation
subtitle: Number of people in emergency accommodation for homeless people, by month, January 2019 to August 2026.

sources.publisher: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage
sources.title: Monthly homelessness reports

key_fact: 17,885 people were in emergency accommodation in August 2026, including 5,830 dependants, almost all of them children. That was up from 9,987 in January 2019.

title: Emergency accommodation by region
subtitle: Number of people in emergency accommodation for homeless people, by region, August 2026.

sources.publisher: Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage
sources.title: Monthly homelessness reports

key_fact: In August 2026, 70% of people in emergency accommodation were in Dublin, 12,429 people.

title: House prices
subtitle: Residential Property Price Index, January 2005 to August 2026. 100 is the average price level in 2015.
key_fact: In August 2026, house prices nationally were 110% above their 2015 average, before adjusting for inflation.

title: Average house price by county
subtitle: Average price paid for homes bought at market value by households, 2010 to 2025. Use the slider to move through the years.

sources.title: Market-based Household Purchases of Residential Dwellings (HPA03)

key_fact: In 2025, the average price paid for a home ranged from €209,300 in Longford to €591,300 in Dublin.

title: Renting by county
subtitle: Percentage of households renting their home, from a private landlord, a local authority or a housing body, Census 2022.

sources.title: Census 2022 Small Area Population Statistics, permanent private households (SAP2022T6T3CTY)

key_fact: At the 2022 census, 38% of households in Dublin rented their home, the highest share of any county, compared with 20% in Meath.

title: Average rent by county
subtitle: Average monthly rent on new private tenancies registered with the Residential Tenancies Board, 2008 to 2025. Use the slider to move through the years.
key_fact: In 2025, the average monthly rent on a new tenancy ranged from €977 in Donegal to €2,159 in Dublin.

title: What everyday items cost
subtitle: Change in the national average price of selected items, October 2021 to October 2026, with the price at each date.
key_fact: Full fat milk cost €2.39 on average in October 2026, up from €1.69 in October 2021, a rise of 41%.

title: Energy prices
subtitle: Consumer prices for electricity, gas, home heating oil and petrol, compared with all items, 2015 average = 100, January 2015 to October 2026.

sources.title: Consumer Price Index, detailed sub indices (CPM24)

key_fact: In October 2026, electricity prices were 91% higher than in 2015, and gas prices 116% higher, compared with 31% for all items.

title: Food prices
subtitle: Consumer prices for food, compared with all items, 2015 average = 100, January 2015 to October 2026.

sources.title: Consumer Price Index, detailed sub indices (CPM24)

key_fact: Food prices were 18% higher in October 2026 than in 2015, compared with 31% for all items. Food prices rose 29% between January 2021 and October 2026, after falling slightly in the years before.

title: Inflation
subtitle: Change in consumer prices compared with the same month a year earlier, November 1996 to October 2026.
key_fact: Consumer prices were 4.3% higher in October 2026 than a year earlier.

title: Price changes by type of spending
subtitle: Change in consumer prices for each main group of goods and services, October 2021 to October 2026.
key_fact: Over the five years to October 2026, prices rose most for housing and energy (+53.2%), compared with +24.0% for all items.

title: Driving to work by county
subtitle: Percentage of people travelling to work who went by car, as a driver or passenger, Census 2022.

sources.title: Census 2022 Small Area Population Statistics, means of travel to work (SAP2022T11T1CTY)

key_fact: At the 2022 census, 80% of people travelling to work in Clare went by car, the highest share of any county. The lowest was Dublin, at 52%.

title: Average weekly earnings
subtitle: Average weekly earnings of employees, in cash terms and adjusted for consumer prices (in 2026 Q2 prices), 2008 Q1 to 2026 Q2.

sources.title: Average Earnings, Hours Worked, Employment and Labour Costs (EHQ03)

key_fact: Average weekly earnings were €1,047 in 2026 Q2, 3.9% higher than a year earlier, or 0.3% higher after adjusting for prices.

title: GDP and modified gross national income
subtitle: Gross domestic product (GDP) and modified gross national income (GNI*) in billions of euro at current prices, 1995 to 2025.

sources.title: Modified Gross National Income at Current Market Prices (NA001)

key_fact: In 2025, GNI* was €334 billion, 55% of GDP.

title: Disposable income per person by county
subtitle: Average household disposable income per person in each county, in euro at current prices, 2000 to 2024. Use the slider to move through the years.
key_fact: In 2024, disposable income per person ranged from €23,725 in Longford to €33,889 in Dublin, compared with €30,139 for the State.

title: Unemployment rate
subtitle: Percentage of people in the labour force who are unemployed, seasonally adjusted, January 1998 to October 2026.
key_fact: The unemployment rate was 4.8% in October 2026, seasonally adjusted.

title: Working from home by county
subtitle: Percentage of people at work who said they worked from home for at least part of the week, Census 2022.

sources.title: Census 2022 Small Area Population Statistics, working from home (SAP2022T11T4CTY)

key_fact: At the 2022 census, 46% of people at work in Dublin worked from home for at least part of the week, the highest share of any county, compared with 23% in Monaghan.

title: Leaving Certificate candidates
subtitle: Number of people who sat the Leaving Certificate (secondary school), school years 1999-2000 to 2023-2024.

sources.title: Junior and Leaving Certificate Examination Candidates (Number) (EDA93)

key_fact: 60,839 people sat the Leaving Certificate in the 2023-2024 school year.

title: Leaving Certificate subjects taken at higher level
subtitle: Percentage of Leaving Certificate (secondary school) candidates in the ten largest subjects who took the higher-level paper rather than the ordinary-level paper, 2024.
key_fact: In 2024, 39% of Leaving Cert Mathematics candidates took the higher-level paper, the lowest share of the ten largest subjects.

title: Average class size in primary schools
subtitle: Average number of pupils in a mainstream class in primary schools, school years 2003-2004 to 2024-2025.

sources.title: Average Class Size in Mainstream National Schools (EDA21)

key_fact: The average primary school class had 22.2 pupils in 2024-2025, down from 24.9 in 2014-2015.

title: Pupils in primary and secondary schools
subtitle: Number of pupils in primary schools and in secondary (second-level) schools aided by the Department of Education, school years 1999-2000 to 2025-2026.

sources.title: Pupils Enrolled in Second Level Schools (EDA70)

key_fact: In the 2025-2026 school year there were 545,726 pupils in primary schools and 429,653 in secondary schools. Primary numbers peaked in 2018-2019, at 567,772.

title: Young adults with a third-level qualification
subtitle: Percentage of people aged 30 to 34 with a third-level qualification, Ireland and the 27 EU countries, 2021 to 2025.

sources.title: Persons aged 30-34 years with a Third Level Education in EU Member States (EATR04)

key_fact: In 2025, 69% of people aged 30 to 34 in Ireland had a third-level qualification, compared with an EU average of 46%.

title: Students in third-level education
subtitle: Number of students enrolled in third-level education (universities, technological universities and colleges), academic years 2014-2015 to 2025-2026.

sources.title: Students enrolled in third level education (MIP41)

key_fact: 283,950 students were enrolled in third-level education in 2025-2026, up from 214,590 in 2014-2015.

title: Assaults, threats and harassment offences by Garda division
subtitle: Recorded assaults, threats and harassment offences per 1,000 people in each Garda division, 2025.

sources.title: Recorded crime incidents by Garda station (CJA07)
Census of Population, population by county (F1001)

key_fact: In 2025, the Westmeath division had the highest rate of recorded assaults, threats and harassment offences, 7.1 per 1,000 people, compared with 2.8 in the Meath division.

title: Burglaries by Garda division
subtitle: Recorded burglaries per 1,000 people in each Garda division, 2025.

sources.title: Recorded crime incidents by Garda station (CJA07)
Census of Population, population by county (F1001)

key_fact: In 2025, the Dublin Metropolitan Region and the Wicklow division had the joint highest rate of recorded burglaries, 2.6 per 1,000 people, compared with 0.5 in the Mayo division.

title: Recorded crime by type of offence
subtitle: Number of crime incidents recorded by An Garda Síochána in 2025, by type of offence.
key_fact: Theft was the most common type of recorded crime in 2025, with 73,564 incidents, about 26% of the offences shown.

title: Recorded thefts and burglaries
subtitle: Number of theft and burglary incidents recorded by An Garda Síochána each year, by type, 2003 to 2025.
key_fact: 34,312 thefts from shops were recorded in 2025, compared with 15,692 in 2003.

title: Recorded crime over time
subtitle: Number of crime incidents recorded by An Garda Síochána each year, for the five largest types of crime against people and property, 2003 to 2025.
key_fact: 8,466 burglaries were recorded in 2025, down from a peak of 28,473 in 2012.

title: People born abroad by county
subtitle: Percentage of people usually living in each county who were born outside Ireland, Census 2022.

sources.title: Census 2022 Small Area Population Statistics, birthplace (SAP2022T2T1CTY)

key_fact: At the 2022 census, 25% of people living in Dublin were born outside Ireland, the highest share of any county, compared with 14% in Kilkenny.

title: Where people came from and went to
subtitle: Estimated number of immigrants by the country or region they came from, and emigrants by where they went, in the twelve months to April 2026.
key_fact: In the twelve months to April 2026, the largest group of emigrants, 14,600 people, went to the other countries that were EU members before 2004.

title: People moving to and from Ireland
subtitle: Estimated number of people who moved to Ireland (immigrants) and who left (emigrants) in the twelve months to April, 1987 to 2026.
key_fact: In the twelve months to April 2026, an estimated 110,600 people moved to Ireland and 62,500 left. Emigration was highest in 2012, at 83,000.

title: Deaths from heart disease, cancer and tuberculosis
subtitle: Deaths per 100,000 people each year from heart disease, cancer and tuberculosis, 1922 to 2023.
key_fact: The death rate from tuberculosis fell from 153 per 100,000 people in 1922 to 0.3 in 2023. Cancer has caused more deaths than heart disease in every year since 2003.

title: Distance to hospital emergency department by county
subtitle: Median distance by road from people's homes to the nearest hospital emergency department, in kilometres, 2026.

sources.title: Average distance to the nearest service for individuals and households by County (MDSI05)

key_fact: In 2026, half of people in Monaghan lived more than 44.2 km by road from a hospital emergency department, the furthest of any county, compared with 13.3 km across the State.

title: Distance to GP by county
subtitle: Median distance by road from people's homes to the nearest GP, in kilometres, 2026.

sources.title: Average distance to the nearest service for individuals and households by County (MDSI05)

key_fact: In 2026, half of people in Roscommon lived more than 5.3 km by road from a GP, the furthest of any county, compared with 1.3 km across the State.

title: Time spent in emergency departments
subtitle: Hours within which half of patients, and 95% of patients, left a public hospital emergency department after arriving, by month, January 2016 to December 2025.

sources.title: Patient experience time in emergency departments (KTA03)

key_fact: In 2025, half of patients left the emergency department within 5.0 hours, but one in twenty spent more than 20 hours there.

title: Life expectancy in Ireland and the EU
subtitle: Life expectancy at birth in years, Ireland and the 27 EU countries, 2018 to 2024.
key_fact: Life expectancy at birth in Ireland was 83.1 years in 2024, compared with an EU average of 81.5 years.

title: Outpatient waiting times
subtitle: Percentage of people on the hospital outpatient waiting list who had been waiting less than 15 months, July 2021 to September 2024.
key_fact: In September 2024, 88% of people on the outpatient waiting list had been waiting less than 15 months, up from 65% in July 2021.

title: Spending on health care
subtitle: Current spending on health care in Ireland, by the State and by households and insurers, € billion, 2000 to 2024.
key_fact: Current spending on health care was €36.3 billion in 2024, of which €28.2 billion (78%) was public. That was 11.3% of GNI*.

title: Patients waiting on trolleys
subtitle: Average number of admitted patients waiting on trolleys in public hospital emergency departments at 8am each day, by month, January 2016 to December 2025.

sources.title: Admitted Patients Waiting on Trolleys in Public Acute Hospital Emergency Departments at 8 am (KTA02)

key_fact: On an average morning in 2025, 265 admitted patients were waiting on trolleys in emergency departments. The highest single count was 804, on 3 January 2023.

title: Greenhouse gas emissions by sector
subtitle: Ireland's greenhouse gas emissions in millions of tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, by sector, 1990 to 2024.
key_fact: Ireland's greenhouse gas emissions were 53.8 million tonnes in 2024, down from a peak of 70.8 million tonnes in 2001. Agriculture was the largest source, at 38% of the total.

title: Emissions per person in Ireland and the EU
subtitle: Greenhouse gas emissions per person in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, Ireland and the 27 EU countries, 2008 to 2024.
key_fact: In 2024, emissions were 10.0 tonnes per person in Ireland, compared with an EU average of 6.7 tonnes.

title: Forest cover by county
subtitle: Forests and woodland as a percentage of each county's area, 2021.

sources.title: Extent of Forests and Woodlands (as a percent of total county area) (FAW02)

key_fact: In 2021, Wicklow had the highest share of its land under forest or woodland, 20.7%, and Meath the lowest, 3.7%.

title: How often Irish speakers speak Irish
subtitle: People aged 3 and over who said they could speak Irish, by how often they speak it, Census 2022.

sources.title: Irish speakers aged 3 years and over (F8001)

key_fact: At the 2022 census, 1,873,997 people said they could speak Irish, and 71,968 (4% of them) said they spoke it every day outside school.

title: Daily Irish speakers in the Gaeltacht
subtitle: Percentage of people aged 3 and over in each Gaeltacht area who speak Irish every day outside school, Census 2011, 2016 and 2022.

sources.title: Daily Irish speakers aged 3 years and over (F8033)

key_fact: In 2022, 31% of people in the Gaeltacht spoke Irish every day outside school, compared with 35% in 2011.

title: Irish speakers by county
subtitle: Percentage of people aged 3 and over who said they could speak Irish, Census 2022.

sources.title: Census 2022 Small Area Population Statistics, ability to speak Irish (SAP2022T3T1CTY)

key_fact: At the 2022 census, 49% of people aged 3 and over in Galway said they could speak Irish, the highest share of any county, compared with 35% in Louth.

title: Government surplus or deficit
subtitle: General government surplus (above zero) or deficit (below zero), € billion, 1995 to 2025.
key_fact: The State had a surplus of €10.7 billion in 2025. The largest deficit was €53.8 billion, in 2010.

title: Government debt
subtitle: Gross general government debt at the end of each year, € billion, 2000 to 2025.

sources.title: General Government Gross and Net Debt ESA2010 (GFA13)
Modified Gross National Income at Current Market Prices (NA001)

key_fact: Government debt was €210 billion at the end of 2025, or 63% of GNI*. Relative to GNI*, it peaked in 2012 at 164%.

title: Where the State's money comes from
subtitle: General government revenue by source, € billion, 2025.

sources.title: General Government: Detailed classification of revenue and output (GFA03)

key_fact: In 2025 the State raised €145 billion. Income tax brought in €36.9 billion and corporation tax €32.9 billion, together almost half of the total.

title: What the State spends money on
subtitle: General government spending by type, € billion, 2025.

sources.title: General Government: Detailed classification of expenditure and consumption (GFA04)

key_fact: The State spent €134 billion in 2025. The largest share, €43.8 billion (33%), went on social welfare and other benefits.

title: The three biggest taxes
subtitle: Revenue from income tax, corporation tax and VAT, € billion, 2000 to 2025.

sources.title: General Government: Detailed classification of revenue and output (GFA03)

key_fact: Corporation tax brought in €32.9 billion in 2025, up from €3.9 billion in 2000.

title: Electric cars in Ireland and the EU
subtitle: Fully electric cars as a share of new passenger cars registered, EU countries, 2024.

sources.title: Electric Passenger Vehicles, Ireland and EU (TEA30)

key_fact: In 2024, 14.2% of new cars registered in Ireland were fully electric, compared with 13.5% across the EU. Ireland had the 11th highest share of the 27 countries. Electric cars made up 3.1% of all cars on Irish roads.

title: How people make their journeys
subtitle: Share of all journeys by main mode of travel, 2024.

sources.title: National Travel Survey, distribution of journeys by mode of travel (NTA10)

key_fact: In 2024, 74% of journeys were made by car, 14% on foot, 4% by bus and 2% by bike.

title: New cars by fuel type
subtitle: Share of new private cars licensed for the first time, by fuel, 2015 to 2025.

sources.title: New Vehicles Licensed for the First Time by Fuel Type (TEA17)

key_fact: In 2025, 19% of new cars were fully electric and a further 15% were plug-in hybrids, up from 0.4% and 0.1% in 2015.

subtitle: Number of private cars licensed in Ireland for the first time, 1997 to 2025.

sources.title: Vehicles Licensed for the First Time (TEA01)

key_fact: 120,797 new cars were licensed in 2025, along with 71,604 imported used cars. New car sales peaked in 2000, at 225,269.

title: Public transport journeys each week
subtitle: Passenger journeys per week by bus, rail and Luas, million, average of the last four weeks, 2019 to 2026.
key_fact: In the four weeks to 27 September 2026, Dublin city buses carried an average of 3.9 million passenger journeys a week, rail 1.2 million and Luas 1.2 million.

title: Rail journeys each year
subtitle: Passenger journeys on Iarnród Éireann trains, including the DART, million, 1981 to 2025.
key_fact: There were 55.0 million rail journeys in 2025, the highest number in figures going back to 1981.

subtitle: Number of people killed in road collisions each year, 2000 to 2025.
